comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet plan set, preventing verification of overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, or patios relative to overhead conductors. Both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances for building projections cannot be assessed.

comment: Overhead utility lines exist in the right-of-way along Valley View Road (western boundary per Sheet 4), and buildings are proposed within potential clearance distance (Sheet 9). No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions from outside conductor to buildings are provided, preventing verification of required 7.5-foot and 15-foot clearances.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1 and 2 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way

comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not included in the submitted site plan. The 39-sheet plan set contains no building elevation drawings. Per UCM § 1.10.3, engineered, sealed elevation drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and buildings, including all projections, with dimensioned clearances are required.
applicableAreas: All buildings 1-8

comment: Site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical design plan (Sheet 21) show building locations and site features, but contain no dimension lines or annotations showing distances from outer electric conductors to building edges, projections, or other site features. Required section views and enlarged plan details with dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location are not provided.
applicableAreas: All buildings 1-8 and site structures

comment: Fences are proposed (noted on landscape plan Sheet 31 and landscape calculations Sheet 35), including wooden privacy fences. Existing utility poles are shown on the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) at multiple property boundaries. Without exact measured distances between proposed fence post locations and existing pole locations, the 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Proposed fence post locations throughout property perimeter

comment: Retaining walls are detailed on Sheets 38-39, and overhead electric facilities exist on property boundaries (Sheet 4). However, no dimension lines or clearance annotations show distances from the outside conductor to the outermost edge of any retaining wall. Horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to wall faces cannot be verified without surveyor data and section exhibits.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls throughout site perimeter and around detention pond

comment: Internal driveways and parking areas are proposed (Sheets 9, 11). Overhead utility lines exist on property boundaries (Sheet 4). No vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attachments) to finished driveway/parking grades are provided. Verification of 16-foot minimum (parking without trucks) or 18-foot (areas with truck traffic) clearance requires surveyed conductor elevation data and grading section exhibits not provided.
applicableAreas: Internal driveways, parking areas with overhead electric line proximity

comment: Dimension lines and clearance annotations on submitted plans show distances from property lines, easement boundaries, and pole locations, but do not originate from the outside conductor location. Per UCM § 1.10.3 and the measurement methodology in the regulatory overview, all clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline or easement boundaries. On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension lines must explicitly show origin at conductor position.
applicableAreas: All overhead electric clearance areas

comment: Existing utility poles are shown on Sheet 4 along the western property line within right-of-way. A public sidewalk is proposed along Valley View Road frontage (Sheet 9). Without dimensioned drawings showing exact clearance distances from sidewalk location to pole positions at each property end along right-of-way, the requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Public sidewalk along Valley View Road right-of-way, property end locations

comment: Overhead distribution lines and electric easements (5-foot easements) are shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4). Buildings are positioned within electric easement areas on the site plan (Sheet 9). Without surveyed conductor routing and exact clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to all buildings and site features within the easement, it cannot be definitively verified that customer facilities are not installed beneath or over distribution conductors (absolute prohibition per UCM § 1.10.3) or that 7.5-foot clearance is maintained for items within easements.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, all site features, electric easement areas

comment: No registered surveyor data showing pole locations and mid-span conductor clearances is provided on any submitted sheet. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows surveyed pole locations, but no conductor elevation data. When overhead facilities cross proposed site features (buildings, driveways, parking), surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are required to verify vertical clearances meet minimum requirements. These measurements are absent from the plan set.
applicableAreas: All structures with potential overhead conductor clearance concerns

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees (marked M for Mitigation and PL for Parking Lot types) positioned within approximately 10-15 feet of the overhead electric line on the southern property boundary. The landscape calculations (Sheet 35) provide a plant list (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but the specific tree species cannot be cross-referenced to the landscape plan location symbols. Without confirmed species identification for the trees near the overhead line, utility-compatible status cannot be verified against ECM Appendix F. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors must be utility-compatible species (generally mature height ≤20 feet marked UC).
applicableAreas: Landscape areas near overhead electric line on southern property boundary

comment: Landscape plan shows proposed trees at 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor running along southern property boundary. Cedar Elm (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible) specified on plant schedule are proposed as part of the mitigation trees. Trees must be repositioned to maintain minimum 15 lateral feet from outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.10.4, or species must be changed to utility-compatible alternatives.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line

comment: Proposed large trees (Cedar Elm at 90 feet mature height, Live Oak at 60 feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are located 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. Large trees require minimum 25 lateral feet clearance from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Trees must be repositioned or replaced with trees of compliant mature height (less than 40 feet).
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line

comment: Electrical utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or landscape plan (Sheet 31). Proposed trees must maintain minimum 10 lateral feet from utility pole centerlines per UCM § 1.10.10.4, but this cannot be verified from submitted plans. Provide pole locations and identify all utility poles on the landscape plan with tree locations relative to poles clearly dimensioned or noted.
applicableAreas: Site-wide utility infrastructure

comment: Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2 and 8, east of Buildings 4 and 7), but landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not provide cross-reference or clear notation showing tree locations relative to transformer access doors. Trees must maintain 10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment access doors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension or cross-sheet reference showing tree clearances from transformer pads.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations

comment: Electrical plan shows underground conduits and pull boxes routing through the site, but specific coordinates or dimensions for underground electrical equipment are not provided on the landscape plan. Trees must maintain minimum 5 lateral feet clearance from underground electrical equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed overlay or dimension showing tree locations relative to all underground electrical equipment with 5-foot clearances verified.
applicableAreas: Underground electrical equipment locations

comment: Underground electrical equipment locations are not detailed on landscape plan, preventing verification of which trees fall within the 20-foot root barrier zone. Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed location plan showing underground equipment, 20-foot zones, tree locations, and root barrier specifications for any trees within affected zones.
applicableAreas: Trees proposed within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees near overhead electric line but identifies them only by regulatory category symbols (M, SY, PL, P) with no species names. Plant schedule exists on Sheet 35 listing species, but landscape plan lacks cross-reference linking specific tree symbols to the species identified on the plant schedule. Proposed trees near utilities must be clearly identified by species directly on the landscape plan or through explicit cross-sheet notation.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line

comment: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet) from smaller trees near overhead electric facilities. Trees shown as 'M' symbols provide no indication of which are Cedar Elm (90 ft), Live Oak (60 ft), or smaller species (Mexican Redbud 20 ft, Texas Mountain Laurel 25 ft). Large tree species and mature heights must be clearly noted or indicated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line

comment: Landscape plan does not show dimensioned clearances between proposed trees and overhead electric conductors. While field measurement identifies distances of 3.1 to 6 feet, plan dimensions and notes must clearly show that all clearances are measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline) to the tree trunk center (not canopy edge) per UCM § 1.10.10.4 measurement methodology. Provide dimensions on landscape plan showing tree-to-conductor distances measured from proper reference points.
applicableAreas: Trees near overhead electric line

comment: Landscape plan does not dimension clearances from tree trunks to overhead electric conductors. All clearance measurements must originate from tree trunk center (planting location symbol), not from projected canopy edge per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension lines and notes on landscape plan confirming that clearances are measured from proper reference points.
applicableAreas: Trees near overhead electric line

comment: Landscape plan proposes trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet from distribution conductors and less than 25 feet for large trees) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Variations to standard tree placement distances and non-compatible species designations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide signed approval letter from Austin Energy or revise landscape plan to maintain required clearances.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
